contents.html: This document describes a worked example of a multi-agency certification and accreditation (C&A) process. The objective of this document is to provide a practical example of how to perform multi-agency C&A. The example is based on a project implemented for the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), called Mountain Pass. The project was implemented to improve the El Paso Intelligence Center (EPIC) information system and related communications and to satisfy EPIC's current and anticipated system needs. EPIC is a multi-agency facility managed by DEA, located in El Paso, Texas and supported by personnel from various participating federal agencies. Mountain Pass was certified and accredited by DEA with the participating agencies defining and assisting the certification process and accepting the implemented security features.
contents.html_ja: この文書は、複数機関の認証および認定（C&A）プロセスの実例を説明します。この文書の目的は、複数機関の C&A をどのように実施するかについての実践的な例を示すことです。この例は、麻薬取締局（DEA）向けに実施された Mountain Pass というプロジェクトに基づいています。このプロジェクトは、エルパソ情報センター（EPIC）の情報システムおよび関連する通信を改善し、EPIC の現在および将来想定されるシステムの必要性を満たすために実施されました。EPIC は、テキサス州エルパソにある DEA が管理する複数機関の施設で、参加するさまざまな連邦機関の職員が支援しています。Mountain Pass は、参加機関が認証プロセスを定義して支援し、実装されたセキュリティ機能を受け入れる形で、DEA によって認証および認定されました。

contents.html: This document includes sample tables, reports, outlines, and charters to assist other Federal agencies in their multi-agency C&A efforts. Although this document focuses on the Mountain Pass Project, the lessons learned and general guidelines provide practical guidance to all civil Federal agencies that perform multi-agency C&A. Also, this document focuses on the certification activities.
contents.html_ja: この文書には、他の連邦機関が複数機関の C&A に取り組む際の助けとなるよう、表、報告書、アウトライン、および憲章の例が含まれています。この文書は Mountain Pass プロジェクトに焦点を当てていますが、得られた教訓と一般的なガイドラインは、複数機関の C&A を実施するすべての民間の連邦機関にとって実践的な指針となります。また、この文書は認証の活動に焦点を当てています。

contents.html: This document consists of five sections and seven appendices. The emphasis in the body of the document is how multi-agency C&A may be performed and the appendices provide samples and examples. Section 1 provides an overview of the Mountain Pass Project. Section 2 discusses the security engineering life cycle, the general C&A process, and the EPIC C&A process. Section 3 describes the EPIC system development roles and responsibilities. Section 4 describes the EPIC certification testing and the accreditation documentation. Finally, Section 5 summarizes the lessons learned from the EPIC project. Appendix A includes a security requirements matrix. Appendix B includes a sample letter to the external agencies requesting support on the C&A effort. Appendix C includes a charter for one of the working groups. Appendix D includes the policies, standards, and regulations that were used to develop the EPIC security requirements. Appendix E includes a generic memorandum of understanding. Appendix F lists the C&A tasks and provides a time table for their completion. Finally, appendix G includes a glossary.
contents.html_ja: この文書は 5 つの節と 7 つの付録からなります。本文では複数機関の C&A をどのように実施できるかに重点を置き、付録では見本と例を示します。第 1 節では、Mountain Pass プロジェクトの概要を示します。第 2 節では、セキュリティエンジニアリングのライフサイクル、一般的な C&A プロセス、および EPIC の C&A プロセスを論じます。第 3 節では、EPIC のシステム開発における役割と責任を説明します。第 4 節では、EPIC の認証試験と認定の文書を説明します。最後に、第 5 節では、EPIC プロジェクトで得られた教訓をまとめます。付録 A にはセキュリティ要件マトリックスを収めています。付録 B には、C&A の取り組みへの支援を外部機関に依頼する書簡の例を収めています。付録 C には、ワーキンググループの 1 つの憲章を収めています。付録 D には、EPIC のセキュリティ要件の策定に用いたポリシー、標準、および規則を収めています。付録 E には、一般的な覚書を収めています。付録 F には、C&A のタスクを挙げ、その完了のスケジュールを示します。最後に、付録 G には用語集を収めています。

contents.html: Certification is required by OMB Circular A-130 for all computer applications processing Sensitive Unclassified (hereafter referred to as Sensitive) information. FIPS PUB 102, Guideline to Computer Security Certification and Accreditation, 27 September 1983, was the document used for C&A guidance on the EPIC project. contents.html: Prior to Mountain Pass, C&A activities at EPIC were handled in an informal manner, with no formal process. For example, the majority of the EPIC documentation addressed the day-to-day operation of the facility and the agreements between the various Federal agencies that participate in EPIC. The Mountain Pass C&A process was intended to address Federal, DOJ, and DEA security standards, guidelines, and requirements. Because EPIC is sponsored and operated by multiple Federal agencies, these agencies were requested to actively participate in the Mountain Pass security engineering and C&A activities. This document describes the security activities, C&A program, tasks, and roles that were developed and implemented for the Mountain Pass Project.
contents.html_ja: Mountain Pass 以前の EPIC における C&A の活動は、正式なプロセスのない非公式な形で扱われていました。たとえば、EPIC の文書の大半は、施設の日常的な運用と、EPIC に参加するさまざまな連邦機関の間の取り決めを扱っていました。Mountain Pass の C&A プロセスは、連邦政府、DOJ、および DEA のセキュリティ標準、ガイドライン、および要件に対応することを意図していました。EPIC は複数の連邦機関によって後援され運用されているため、これらの機関には、Mountain Pass のセキュリティエンジニアリングと C&A の活動に積極的に参加することが求められました。この文書は、Mountain Pass プロジェクトのために策定され実施された、セキュリティの活動、C&A プログラム、タスク、および役割を説明します。

contents.html: The system development methodology that was followed at EPIC was a tailored analyze-design-plan-implement approach. First, a detailed functional analysis of the EPIC environment was conducted. The current EPIC environment was analyzed to determine how, why, when, where, and what tasks were being performed, who performed the tasks, and what products were prepared. Specifically, the analysis included a review of all system-related documents, interviews with current and proposed users and system specialists, and observation of the current system operation. The result of the functional analysis was a recommended Functional Architecture which addressed EPIC's functional requirements and alternative design concepts.
contents.html_ja: EPIC で従ったシステム開発手法は、調整された分析・設計・計画・実装のアプローチでした。まず、EPIC の環境について詳細な機能分析を実施しました。現在の EPIC の環境を分析して、どのようなタスクが、どのように、なぜ、いつ、どこで行われているか、誰がそのタスクを行っているか、どのような成果物が作成されているかを明らかにしました。具体的には、この分析には、システムに関するすべての文書の確認、現在および将来の利用者とシステム専門家へのインタビュー、現行システムの運用の観察が含まれていました。機能分析の結果は、EPIC の機能要件と代替の設計概念に対応する、推奨される機能アーキテクチャでした。

contents.html: The EIS certification process was based on the process defined in FIPS PUB 102, Guideline for Computer Security Certification and Accreditation. This standard was used because EPIC is primarily authorized and staffed by Federal civil agencies and the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) is responsible for providing guidance for civil agencies that process Sensitive information.
contents.html_ja: EIS の認証プロセスは、FIPS PUB 102、Guideline for Computer Security Certification and Accreditation に定義されたプロセスに基づいていました。この標準を用いたのは、EPIC が主に連邦の文民機関によって認可され、人員が配置されており、国立標準技術研究所（NIST）が、機微情報を処理する文民機関に対する指針を提供する責任を負っているためです。

contents.html: As defined in FIPS PUB 102, the certification effort is divided into basic evaluation and detailed evaluation. The general distinction between basic and detailed evaluations is that basic evaluation focuses on the overall security functionality. Detailed evaluation focuses on whether specific security features work correctly, satisfy performance criteria, and acceptably resist penetration. The certification process is an iterative process, with previous stages being reentered and the work repeated. For example, during basic evaluation/RAVA, a new security function may be identified that had not been previously documented. Development of a new security function may require a revision to the security boundary defined in the planning stage and repetition of the data collection stages. At the completion of the certification tests, the formal acceptance of system security by the DAA is based on the Security Evaluation Report/Certification Report of Findings and the documentation developed during the system engineering life cycle stages. The DAA for EIS was the Deputy Administrator of DEA.
contents.html_ja: FIPS PUB 102 に定義されているように、認証の作業は基本評価と詳細評価に分けられます。基本評価と詳細評価の一般的な違いは、基本評価が全体的なセキュリティ機能に焦点を当てるのに対し、詳細評価は、個々のセキュリティ機能が正しく動作するか、性能基準を満たすか、および侵入に対して許容できる程度に耐えるかに焦点を当てることです。認証プロセスは反復的なプロセスであり、前の段階に戻って作業を繰り返します。たとえば、基本評価／RAVA の間に、それまで文書化されていなかった新しいセキュリティ機能が特定されることがあります。新しいセキュリティ機能の開発には、計画段階で定義したセキュリティ境界の改訂と、データ収集の段階の繰り返しが必要になる場合があります。認証試験の完了時には、セキュリティ評価報告書／認証所見報告書と、システムエンジニアリングのライフサイクルの各段階で作成した文書に基づいて、DAA がシステムセキュリティを正式に受け入れます。EIS の DAA は、DEA の副長官でした。

contents.html: Due to the nature of DEA's mission and the sensitivity of its data, evaluating system security, implementing appropriate safeguards, and certifying systems are a vital part of DEA's system life cycle development process. Due to EPIC's mission and the sensitivity of its data, security was also important to the agencies that participate at EPIC.
contents.html_ja: DEA の任務の性質とそのデータの機微性のために、システムのセキュリティを評価し、適切な防護策を実装し、システムを認証することは、DEA のシステムライフサイクル開発プロセスの不可欠な部分です。EPIC の任務とそのデータの機微性のために、セキュリティは、EPIC に参加する機関にとっても重要でした。

contents.html: Certification of the EIS involved a technical assessment of the security features/functionality to determine the extent that these features met the EIS and DEA security requirements and applicable security policies (e.g., DOJ, Executive Orders (E.O.s), Privacy Act). Certification also included executing security tests to demonstrate the adequacy of the security features and requirements. Accreditation of the EIS was a management decision by the Deputy Administrator of DEA to operate the EIS in a specific operational environment. The objective of the C&A effort was to accredit the EIS as a partitioned system, physically separated into two regions: a Sensitive region and a Classified region, with a low-to-high security guard connecting the two regions.
contents.html_ja: EIS の認証には、これらのセキュリティ機能が EIS と DEA のセキュリティ要件および適用されるセキュリティポリシー（たとえば、DOJ、大統領令（E.O.）、プライバシー法）をどの程度満たしているかを判断するための、セキュリティ機能の技術的な評価が含まれていました。認証には、セキュリティ機能と要件の妥当性を実証するためのセキュリティ試験の実行も含まれていました。EIS の認定は、特定の運用環境で EIS を運用するという DEA 副長官の管理上の決定でした。C&A の取り組みの目的は、EIS を、機微情報の領域と機密情報の領域という物理的に分離された 2 つの領域からなり、両領域を低位から高位へのセキュリティガードで接続する分割されたシステムとして認定することでした。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像（PDF p.18）と OCR の文字を語ごとに照合。ページまたぎ・行の分断をまとめる。行から外れた DEA・C&A を戻し、ofthe・efifort を直す。

contents.html: For Mountain Pass, RAVA was selected as the basic evaluation methodology. ST&E was selected as the detailed evaluation methodology. Both methodologies assess the adequacy of the security features, but from different perspectives. RAVA focused on the appropriateness of the safeguards to minimize risk and ST&E focused on the functionality and effectiveness of the safeguards.
contents.html_ja: Mountain Pass では、基本評価の手法として RAVA を、詳細評価の手法として ST&E を選びました。どちらの手法もセキュリティ機能の妥当性を評価しますが、観点が異なります。RAVA は、リスクを最小化するうえでの防護策の適切さに焦点を当て、ST&E は、防護策の機能と有効性に焦点を当てました。

contents.html: Phase I certification focused on the existing physical and administrative/personnel security functionality because the number of technical security features that were implemented was limited. In general, the Phase I security features were provided by COTS products. At the completion of Phase I, an interim accreditation from the DAA was requested. This accreditation did not include the MOUs for the external systems because the existing technical data exchange arrangements did not change until Phase II. Goals of the Phase I certification effort were to test the certification process and make refinements, if required. This effort was critical because of the limited time frame for Mountain Pass and the number of C&A tasks that overlapped throughout the project.
contents.html_ja: フェーズ I では、実装された技術的セキュリティ機能の数が限られていたため、認証は既存の物理的セキュリティと管理的・要員セキュリティの機能に焦点を当てました。一般に、フェーズ I のセキュリティ機能は COTS 製品によって提供されました。フェーズ I の完了時に、DAA に暫定認定を要請しました。既存の技術的なデータ交換の取り決めがフェーズ II まで変わらなかったため、この認定には外部システムとの MOU は含まれていませんでした。フェーズ I の認証の目標は、認証プロセスを試行し、必要であれば改良を加えることでした。Mountain Pass の期間が限られており、プロジェクト全体にわたって重なり合う C&A タスクが多数あったため、この取り組みは極めて重要でした。

contents.html: The Senior Management Team met periodically and provided oversight and both general and specific guidance to the Program Management Office (PMO). PMO personnel were provided by DISA and EPIC. The day-to-day activities of the project were directed by a PMO team consisting of a PM, his Deputy, and advisory and administrative staffs. At the working level, the project was composed of a System Engineering Team and an Integration Team. Each team was led by a government Team Chief. Finally, a Transition Team composed of EPIC personnel assisted in the transition of system management and support from the project team to EPIC at the completion of the project.
contents.html_ja: 上級管理チームは定期的に会合を開き、プログラム管理室（PMO）に対して監督と、全般的および個別の指導を行いました。PMO の職員は、DISA と EPIC から提供されました。プロジェクトの日常の活動は、PM、副 PM、および助言・事務のスタッフからなる PMO チームが指揮しました。実務レベルでは、プロジェクトはシステムエンジニアリングチームと統合チームで構成されていました。各チームは、政府のチームチーフが率いていました。最後に、EPIC の職員からなる移行チームが、プロジェクトの完了時に、システムの管理と支援をプロジェクトチームから EPIC に移行する作業を補佐しました。

contents.html: Approximately 80% of the project activity was planned to take place at EPIC. Ideally, both the PM and the Deputy and most of the project team were to reside at EPIC. Most of the technical work was expected to be performed at EPIC, with some work to be performed in the Washington area. In reality, a significant portion of the project work was completed in the Washington area because of better access to vendors and technical knowledge and expertise. The PM was originally intended to be an on-site position, but since the 80% rule was not enforced, the PM worked primarily out of Washington, D.C. to direct the efforts of the integration team and to maintain contact with the SMT. The Deputy PM resided at EPIC.
contents.html_ja: プロジェクト活動の約 80% は EPIC で行われる計画でした。理想的には、PM と副 PM、およびプロジェクトチームの大半が EPIC に常駐することになっていました。技術的な作業の大半は EPIC で実施される見込みで、一部の作業はワシントン地域で実施される予定でした。実際には、ベンダーや技術的な知識・専門性により容易にアクセスできたため、プロジェクトの作業のかなりの部分がワシントン地域で完了しました。PM はもともと現地に常駐する職位とされていましたが、80% の規則が徹底されなかったため、PM は、統合チームの取り組みを指揮し、SMT との連絡を維持するために、主にワシントン D.C. で勤務しました。副 PM は EPIC に常駐しました。

contents.html: EIS security requirements have been described as C2+ because the minimum of C2 functionality was required for the EIS with additional functions found at higher assurance levels in the TCSEC (e.g., audit, configuration management, and security administration). Security requirements were applied to both EIS regions with administrative and operational activities performed on each region because of the separation of the two regions. Both regions operated in system high mode with all users cleared to the highest level of information on the Classified region.
contents.html_ja: EIS のセキュリティ要件は C2+ と表現されてきました。これは、EIS には最低限 C2 の機能が必要とされ、TCSEC のより高い保証レベルにある追加機能（たとえば、監査、構成管理、セキュリティ管理）が加わっていたためです。セキュリティ要件は EIS の両方の領域に適用され、2 つの領域が分離されているため、管理的・運用的な活動は各領域で実施されました。両方の領域は、全利用者に機密領域の情報の最高レベルまでアクセス許可が与えられたシステムハイモードで運用されました。

contents.html: Security Architecture: The EIS security architecture was partitioned, logically and physically, into two separate regions. The first region contained Sensitive information and the second contained Classified information up to the Secret level. The two regions were connected by a one-way Guard (the EPIC Guard) that permitted the one-way flow of information from the Unclassified region to the Classified region. Security architecture diagrams were used to graphically display the configuration that was to be accredited. The architecture diagrams were extremely useful for clearly identifying the external databases and message systems and illustrating the proposed configuration at EPIC. Many versions of the architecture diagrams were developed prior to system accreditation. A generalized version of the EIS Unclassified region is illustrated in figure 4-1 and a generalized version of the Classified region in figure 4-2<sup>1</sup>.
contents.html_ja: セキュリティアーキテクチャ: EIS のセキュリティアーキテクチャは、論理的にも物理的にも 2 つの別々の領域に分割されていました。第 1 の領域は機微情報を含み、第 2 の領域は Secret レベルまでの機密情報を含んでいました。2 つの領域は、非機密領域から機密領域への情報の一方向の流れを許可する一方向ガード（EPIC ガード）で接続されていました。セキュリティアーキテクチャ図は、認定される構成を図示するために用いました。アーキテクチャ図は、外部のデータベースとメッセージシステムを明確に特定し、EPIC での提案された構成を示すうえで、極めて有用でした。システムの認定の前に、アーキテクチャ図の多くの版が作成されました。EIS の非機密領域の一般化した版を図 4-1 に、機密領域の一般化した版を図 4-2<sup>1</sup> に示します。

contents.html: C&A Plan: The EIS C&A Plan described the C&A methodology, the certification tasks, system security plan, and accreditation documentation. The C&A Plan included a detailed list of all the C&A tasks and the organization with primary responsibility for that task (e.g., RAVA contractor, CWG, AWG, ST&E contractor). A sample C&A task schedule, based on the Mountain Pass effort, is included in appendix F of this document. The C&A Plan also described the roles and responsibilities of the CWG, AWG, Integration Contractor, RAVA, ST&E contractor, and the ISSO.
contents.html_ja: C&A 計画: EIS の C&A 計画は、C&A の手法、認証タスク、システムセキュリティ計画、および認定の文書を記述しました。C&A 計画には、すべての C&A タスクの詳細な一覧と、そのタスクを主に担当する組織（たとえば、RAVA 請負業者、CWG、AWG、ST&E 請負業者）が含まれていました。Mountain Pass の取り組みに基づく C&A タスクのスケジュールの例は、この文書の付録 F に収めています。C&A 計画は、CWG、AWG、統合請負業者、RAVA、ST&E 請負業者、および ISSO の役割と責任も記述していました。

contents.html: Included in the C&A Plan was a generic MOU between EPIC and each linked external agency. The MOU documented the security functionality, security procedures, and disclosure of information requirements necessary to allow the exchange of data between EIS and each external system. A generic MOU is included in appendix E of this document. It was the responsibility of each external agency to tailor the generic MOU.
contents.html_ja: C&A 計画には、EPIC と、リンクされた各外部機関との間の一般的な MOU が含まれていました。MOU は、EIS と各外部システムとの間のデータ交換を可能にするために必要な、セキュリティ機能、セキュリティ手順、および情報開示の要件を文書化していました。一般的な MOU は、この文書の付録 E に収めています。一般的な MOU を調整するのは、各外部機関の責任でした。

contents.html: Technical Controls: The technical controls section contained a matrix that allocated the EIS security requirements to the EIS system component where the requirement was implemented (e.g., EPIC Guard, site/procedural). This section also discussed the security capabilities provided by each component as it applied to the major requirements headings (e.g., DAC, audit, system state, data integrity).
contents.html_ja: 技術的管理策: 技術的管理策の節には、EIS のセキュリティ要件を、その要件が実装される EIS のシステムコンポーネント（たとえば、EPIC ガード、サイト／手続）に割り当てるマトリックスが含まれていました。この節では、主要な要件の見出し（たとえば、DAC、監査、システム状態、データの完全性）に関して各コンポーネントが提供するセキュリティ能力も論じました。

contents.html: The EIS Security Policy and Procedures document (EIS SP&P) outlined the security controls implemented by EPIC to safeguard all Sensitive and Classified information assets and materials. The EIS SP&P document also established guidelines and responsibilities for the protection of EPIC information assets. The purpose of the EIS SP&P document was to describe the security-related policies, procedures, and responsibilities for protecting Classified and Sensitive information stored, processed, or handled by the EIS.
contents.html_ja: EIS セキュリティポリシーおよび手順の文書（EIS SP&P）は、機微および機密の情報資産と資料のすべてを保護するために EPIC が実装したセキュリティ管理策の概要を示しました。EIS SP&P の文書は、EPIC の情報資産の保護に関するガイドラインと責任も定めていました。EIS SP&P の文書の目的は、EIS が保存、処理、または取り扱う機密情報と機微情報を保護するための、セキュリティ関連のポリシー、手順、および責任を記述することでした。

contents.html: Individuals representing all agencies participating in the EPIC project were interviewed to identify the primary lessons learned during the development and acquisition process. These lessons learned are divided into two areas: management and technical and are summarized in sections 5.1 and 5.2. Activities/processes that worked well and those that did not are included.
contents.html_ja: 開発と調達のプロセスの間に得られた主な教訓を特定するために、EPIC プロジェクトに参加したすべての機関を代表する個人に聞き取りを行いました。得られた教訓は、管理と技術の 2 つの領域に分けられ、5.1 節と 5.2 節にまとめています。うまくいった活動／プロセスと、うまくいかなかったものの両方を含めています。

contents.html: Senior Management Team: The SMT functioned as the planning and decision-making group responsible for ensuring adherence to the Mountain Pass activities. The SMT provided the appropriate level of management authority and political clout to make decisions and ensure that the project progressed on schedule and within budget. The SMT was an effective organization because it provided significant management oversight and made decisions when requested. For example, the SMT was very responsive to the PM's needs and requests for formal direction.
contents.html_ja: 上級管理チーム: SMT は、Mountain Pass の活動が遵守されることを確実にする責任を負う、計画と意思決定のグループとして機能しました。SMT は、決定を下し、プロジェクトがスケジュールどおり予算内で進むことを確実にするために、適切な水準の管理権限と政治的影響力を提供しました。SMT は、重要な管理上の監督を提供し、求められたときに決定を下したため、有効な組織でした。たとえば、SMT は、PM のニーズと正式な指示の要請に非常に迅速に対応しました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像（PDF p.45）と OCR の文字を語ごとに照合。斜体を付ける。

contents.html: Program Management: The PMO was an effective manager of a multitude of simultaneous contracts and contractors, and government personnel. The PMO enthusiastically participated in and encouraged the exchange of information among the various Mountain Pass participants, worked effectively with the SMT in resolving issues and recommending solutions, and clearly communicated the delivery dates and products needed. This kept the project on schedule and within budget. Having an on-site coordinator (the Deputy PM) was extremely important because it facilitated the early identification of problems and their rapid resolution. It also provided the on-site teams with the appropriate level of authority and guidance necessary to ensure decisions were made and implemented correctly.
contents.html_ja: プログラム管理: PMO は、同時に進行する多数の契約、請負業者、および政府職員を有効に管理しました。PMO は、Mountain Pass の各参加者の間の情報交換に熱心に参加してこれを促し、課題の解決と解決策の推奨において SMT と効果的に連携し、必要な納期と成果物を明確に伝えました。これにより、プロジェクトはスケジュールどおり予算内で進みました。現地の調整役（副 PM）がいたことは極めて重要でした。問題の早期の特定と迅速な解決が容易になったためです。また、決定が正しく行われ実施されることを確実にするために必要な、適切な水準の権限と指導を、現地のチームに与えました。

contents.html: Accreditation Working Group (AWG): The AWG facilitated communications between participants and helped to raise security issues early. A great deal of informal communications between AWG members helped to get issues raised and solved in an open environment. All meetings were well documented and information was always readily available and distributed to all participants. The AWG was a key success factor because all members actively participated, were energetic and positive, and caused necessary actions to happen quickly. AWG members also provided significant technical expertise when requested, resulting in well-informed discussions and decisions at the meetings. Another critical success factor was continuity of the membership - the majority of the AWG members participated from the beginning to the end of the Mountain Pass Project and members who were replaced were provided with all the documentation to bring them up to speed.
contents.html_ja: 認定ワーキンググループ（AWG）: AWG は、参加者間の意思疎通を円滑にし、セキュリティ上の課題を早期に提起する助けとなりました。AWG のメンバー間の多くの非公式な意思疎通が、課題を率直な環境で提起し解決する助けとなりました。すべての会合は十分に文書化され、情報は常にすぐに入手でき、すべての参加者に配布されました。AWG は、すべてのメンバーが積極的に参加し、精力的で前向きであり、必要な行動を速やかに実現させたため、成功の重要な要因でした。AWG のメンバーは、求められたときに重要な技術的専門性も提供し、会合で十分な情報に基づく議論と決定が行われました。もう 1 つの重要な成功要因は、構成員の継続性でした。AWG のメンバーの大半は、Mountain Pass プロジェクトの最初から最後まで参加し、交代したメンバーには、状況に追いつけるようにすべての文書が提供されました。

contents.html: Certification Working Group (CWG): This group was established to provide technical guidance and recommendations to the AWG and the contractors. However, because most of the CWG members also participated in the AWG, this group met only a couple of times. At times, the AWG meetings were lengthy because a detailed analysis of an issue with recommended alternatives was not provided. These analyses should have been developed by the CWG.
contents.html_ja: 認証ワーキンググループ（CWG）: このグループは、AWG と請負業者に技術的な指導と推奨事項を提供するために設置されました。しかし、CWG のメンバーの大半は AWG にも参加していたため、このグループは数回しか会合を開きませんでした。ある課題について、推奨される代替案を伴う詳細な分析が提供されなかったために、AWG の会合が長引くこともありました。これらの分析は、CWG が作成すべきでした。

contents.html: Integration Contractor: The integration contractor was provided a detailed system design and, therefore, was able to develop a relatively rapid COTS solution. They were responsive to the sponsor and the users in modifying the implementation to provide an acceptable user interface. One of the major lessons learned was that the implementation of the security features should have occurred much earlier in the implementation effort. This resulted in a crunch in the schedule and less time to complete the RAVA and ST&E tasks.
contents.html_ja: 統合請負業者: 統合請負業者には詳細なシステム設計が提供されたため、比較的迅速に COTS の解決策を開発することができました。統合請負業者は、許容できる利用者インタフェースを提供するために実装を修正する際、スポンサーと利用者に迅速に対応しました。得られた主な教訓の 1 つは、セキュリティ機能の実装は、実装の取り組みのもっと早い時期に行うべきだったということです。これにより、スケジュールが逼迫し、RAVA と ST&E のタスクを完了する時間が少なくなりました。

contents.html: Memorandums of Understanding (MOUs): The MOU process was the most difficult problem for the AWG members to finish. Even with extensive information sharing, it appeared that there were many distinct differences in the way law enforcement agencies protect information. There were no consistent information processing standards for law enforcement agencies. The MOUs should have been started sooner (at the beginning of the project) when all the AWG representatives were initially selected. Also, the MOU process was impacted by the requirement to have the agreements signed by the agency legal representatives. This extended the time to completion.
contents.html_ja: 覚書（MOU）: MOU のプロセスは、AWG のメンバーが完了させるうえで最も困難な問題でした。広範な情報共有を行ったにもかかわらず、法執行機関が情報を保護する方法には多くの明確な違いがあるように見えました。法執行機関に共通する情報処理の標準はありませんでした。MOU は、すべての AWG の代表者が最初に選ばれた時点（プロジェクトの開始時）に、もっと早く着手すべきでした。また、MOU のプロセスは、合意書に各機関の法務担当者の署名を得るという要件の影響を受けました。これにより、完了までの時間が延びました。

contents.html: Software Engineering: The DBMS and user interface software were primarily developed at the integration contractor facility in the Washington, D.C. area. Because there was minimal interaction and communication with users at EPIC, significant changes had to be made when the implementation was demonstrated to the users. Also, it was more difficult to accommodate complex (and sometimes varying) user requirements from a distance.
contents.html_ja: ソフトウェアエンジニアリング: DBMS と利用者インタフェースのソフトウェアは、主にワシントン D.C. 地域にある統合請負業者の施設で開発されました。EPIC の利用者との相互作用と意思疎通が最小限であったため、実装を利用者に実演した際に、大幅な変更を行わなければなりませんでした。また、複雑な（ときには変動する）利用者の要件に、離れた場所から対応することは、より困難でした。

contents.html: Basic and Detailed Evaluation: ST&E was extremely effective as the detailed evaluation methodology. The ST&E team used the security requirements and the results of the RAVA tasks as the basis for developing the security and certification tests. This provided continuity and traceability. The RAVA methodology was most effective in identifying the primary security vulnerabilities and risks.
contents.html_ja: 基本評価と詳細評価: ST&E は、詳細評価の手法として極めて有効でした。ST&E チームは、セキュリティ要件と RAVA タスクの結果を、セキュリティ試験と認証試験を作成する際の基礎として用いました。これにより、継続性と追跡可能性が確保されました。RAVA の手法は、主なセキュリティ上の脆弱性とリスクを特定するうえで最も有効でした。

contents.html: Security-Related Issues: It is important to define security requirements early, with a special focus on audit requirements because of storage and performance implications. The specification of security requirements will assist in the selection of COTS products. Divide security requirements into categories and assign individual responsibility for identifying and validating security requirements by category. Identify those security requirements which are mandatory (non-negotiable) versus those which can be delayed. This information may be used in the selection of the integration contractor and COTS products.
contents.html_ja: セキュリティ関連の課題: 保存容量と性能への影響があるため特に監査要件に重点を置いて、セキュリティ要件を早期に定義することが重要です。セキュリティ要件の仕様化は、COTS 製品の選定に役立ちます。セキュリティ要件をカテゴリに分け、カテゴリごとにセキュリティ要件を特定し、妥当性を確認する責任者を割り当ててください。必須（交渉不可）のセキュリティ要件と、後回しにできるセキュリティ要件を特定してください。この情報は、統合請負業者と COTS 製品の選定に用いることができます。

contents.html: The Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) embarked on a project to modernize and improve the El Paso Intelligence Center’s (EPIC) information processing capability. This project is called the Mountain Pass Project and involves your agency. The objective of the project is to provide the DEA/EPIC with an improved, integrated, and automated information system in 1992. The EPIC Information System (EIS) is intended to meet or exceed current information processing needs of DEA/EPIC and participating agencies, as well as provide the infrastructure from which information system requirements may be met.
contents.html_ja: 麻薬取締局（DEA）は、エルパソ情報センター（EPIC）の情報処理能力を近代化し改善するプロジェクトに着手しました。このプロジェクトは Mountain Pass プロジェクトと呼ばれ、貴機関も関わっています。このプロジェクトの目的は、1992 年に、改善された統合された自動化情報システムを DEA/EPIC に提供することです。EPIC 情報システム（EIS）は、DEA/EPIC と参加機関の現在の情報処理のニーズを満たすか上回るとともに、情報システムの要件を満たすことができる基盤を提供することを意図しています。

contents.html: It is not the intention of this project to alter or disrupt the information sharing relationships that had been established between the DEA/EPIC and the participating agencies. These relationships have served the counternarcotics efforts well and were deemed to be mutually beneficial to all DEA/EPIC participating agencies. However, we will need to properly document these information sharing relationships which developed and evolved informally over the years.
contents.html_ja: このプロジェクトは、DEA/EPIC と参加機関の間で確立されてきた情報共有の関係を変えたり妨げたりすることを意図していません。これらの関係は、麻薬対策の取り組みによく役立ってきており、DEA/EPIC に参加するすべての機関にとって相互に有益であると考えられてきました。ただし、長年にわたって非公式に発展し進化してきたこれらの情報共有の関係を、適切に文書化する必要があります。

contents.html: An important part of this project is the information systems certification and accreditation (C&A) process that is required by OMB Circular A-130. Certification is the technical evaluation of a system (the EIS in this case) to determine how effectively it meets information security requirements. Accreditation is the acknowledgment and acceptance of residual information security risks and the decision and authorization to operate the system in the manner for which it was intended. In order to ensure that the needed information security posture is achieved, a Certification Working Group (CWG) and an Accreditation Working Group (AWG) have been established. The CWG, for the most part, consists of technical experts who will assess risks to the EIS, analyze the vulnerabilities of the EIS, and recommend balanced actions to mitigate information security weaknesses.
contents.html_ja: このプロジェクトの重要な部分は、OMB Circular A-130 が求める情報システムの認証および認定（C&A）プロセスです。認証とは、システム（この場合は EIS）が情報セキュリティ要件をどの程度有効に満たしているかを判断するための、システムの技術的な評価です。認定とは、残留する情報セキュリティリスクを認識して受け入れ、システムを意図された方法で運用することを決定し、許可することです。必要な情報セキュリティの態勢を確実に達成するため、認証ワーキンググループ（CWG）と認定ワーキンググループ（AWG）が設置されています。CWG は、大部分が技術の専門家で構成され、EIS のリスクを評価し、EIS の脆弱性を分析し、情報セキュリティ上の弱点を緩和するためのバランスの取れた措置を勧告します。

contents.html: The purpose of the AWG is to ensure that the information security concerns of all agencies that provide information to the DEA/EPIC are adequately addressed in the EIS. To meet this objective, the AWG is briefed monthly and from an information security standpoint, monitors the progress of the Mountain Pass Project and the results of the certification process. In addition, the AWG representatives are requested to provide input and feedback from their agencies on the topics discussed at the monthly meetings. The AWG representatives are also asked to raise any issues that may impact on the timely accreditation of the EIS.
contents.html_ja: AWG の目的は、DEA/EPIC に情報を提供するすべての機関の情報セキュリティ上の懸念が、EIS で適切に対処されることを確実にすることです。この目的を達成するため、AWG は毎月説明を受け、情報セキュリティの観点から、Mountain Pass プロジェクトの進捗と認証プロセスの結果を監視します。さらに、AWG の代表者は、毎月の会合で議論された事項について、自機関からの意見とフィードバックを提供することが求められます。AWG の代表者は、EIS の適時の認定に影響を与える可能性のある課題を提起することも求められます。

contents.html: The purpose of the Committee is to review, recommend, monitor, and advise on major security considerations due to technology changes in information systems development. This includes evaluating the extent to which these changes will be implemented and describing the security implications of these changes. The Committee is responsible for developing a strategy to assure that security methods, techniques, plans, and procedures keep pace with the changing technology and that security continues to be an integral element in the planning and implementation of all future systems.
contents.html_ja: 委員会の目的は、情報システムの開発における技術の変化に伴う主要なセキュリティ上の考慮事項について、確認し、勧告し、監視し、助言することです。これには、これらの変化が実装される範囲を評価し、その変化のセキュリティ上の意味を記述することが含まれます。委員会は、セキュリティの手法、技法、計画、および手順が技術の変化に遅れずに対応し、将来のすべてのシステムの計画と実装においてセキュリティが引き続き不可欠な要素であることを確実にするための戦略を策定する責任を負います。

This National Institute of Standards and Technology Interagency Report (NISTIR) presents a practical example on how to perform multi-agency certification and accreditation (C&A).

The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) makes no claim or endorsement of this C&A method. However, as this material may be of use to other organizations, NIST participated in producing and printing the document to make the lessons learned publicly available and to provide for broad dissemination ofthis federally sponsored work. This publication is part of a continuing effort to assist federal agencies in accordance with NIST’s mandate under the Computer Security Act of 1987.
NIST expresses its appreciation to the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) for their contributions to this report.

Questions regarding this publication should be addressed to the Computer Security Division, National Computer Systems Laboratory, Building 225, Room B221, National Institute of Standards and Technology, Gaithersburg, MD, 20899.

This document describes a worked example of a multi-agency certification and accreditation (C&A) process. The objective ofthis document is to provide a practical example of how to perform multi-agency C&A. The example is based on a project implemented for the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), called Mountain Pass. The project was implemented to improve the El Paso Intelligence Center (EPIC) information system and related communications and to satisfy EPIC's current and anticipated system needs. EPIC is a multi-agency facility managed by DEA, located in El Paso, Texas and supported by personnel from various

participating federal agencies. Mountain Pass was certified and accredited by with the participating agencies defining and assisting the certification process and accepting the implemented security features.

The Mountain Pass Project was completed in November 1992 and was managed jointly by the Department of Justice (DOJ), DEA, the Department of Defense (DOD), and the Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA). DISA was the Project Manager (PM) and DEA was the Deputy PM.
This document includes sample tables, reports, outlines, and charters to assist other Federal

agencies in their multi-agency efforts. Although this document focuses on the Mountain Pass Project, the lessons learned and general guidelines provide practical guidance to all civil Federal agencies that perform multi-agency C&A. Also, this document focuses on the certification activities.

This document consists of five sections and seven appendices. The emphasis in the body of the document is how multi-agency C&A may be performed and the appendices provide samples and examples. Section 1 provides an overview of the Mountain Pass Project. Section 2 discusses the security engineering life cycle, the general C&A process, and the EPIC C&A process. Section 3 describes the EPIC system development roles and responsibilities. Section 4 describes the EPIC certification testing and the accreditation documentation. Finally, Section 5 summarizes the lessons learned fi'om the EPIC project. Appendk A includes a security requirements matrix. Appendix B includes a sample letter to the external agencies requesting support on the C&A effort. Appendix C includes a charter for one ofthe working groups. Appendix D includes the policies, standards, and regulations that were used to develop the EPIC security requirements. Appendk E includes a generic memorandum ofunderstanding. Appendix F lists the C&A tasks
and provides a time table for their completion. Finally, appendk includes a glossary.
1.1 EPIC and the Mountain Pass Project
EPIC is supported by personnel from various participating agencies (e.g.. Federal Aviation Administration, United States (U.S.) Coast Guard, U.S. Customs Service). Its mission is to
provide intelligence on drug movement throughout the world by land, sea, and air that is relevant to the United States. EPIC's functions are to:
Provide time-sensitive intelligence support to Law Enforcement Agencies (LEAs). For example, act as a clearing house for suspect information
Maintain an intelligence baseline on drug movement information

The EPIC Information System (EIS) Mountain Pass Project established the first increment of an objective architecture to upgrade and improve the existing system. The Mountain Pass project was itself divided into two phases. The focus of Mountain Pass was to upgrade the existing system and integrate existing database files.
Mountain Pass served the following functions:
Integrated stand-alone automated data processing (ADP) systems and communications links
Consolidated existing files into a database management system (DBMS) - (EPIC Internal Database (EID))
Defined an objective system architecture for the mid-1990's
Provided EPIC with an improved, integrated information system by building the initial increment of the objective architecture
Defined a strategy for getting from Mountain Pass to the objective system

The EIS provided enhanced and integrated capabilities which could be tailored to the needs of authorized EPIC users. EIS was built using open system principles that support the future integration of commercial or Government-developed products. Commercial-ofif-the-shelf (COTS) hardware and software products satisfied most EPIC needs for automated support.
1.2 Scope of the Mountain Pass Security Effort

Certification is required by Circular A- 130 for all computer applications processing Sensitive Unclassified (hereafter referred to as Sensitive) information. FIPS PUB 102, Guideline to Computer Security Certification andAccreditation, 27 September 1983, was the document used for C&A guidance on the EPIC project. FIPS PUB 102 presents, in detail, an approach to developing a program and performing a technical process for certifying and accrediting Sensitive applications.

Prior to Mountain Pass, C&A activities at EPIC were handled in an informal manner, with no formal process. For example, the majority of the EPIC documentation addressed the day-to-day operation of the facility and the agreements between the various Federal agencies that participate

in EPIC. The Mountain Pass process was intended to address Federal, DOT, and security standards, guidelines, and requirements. Because EPIC is sponsored and operated by multiple Federal agencies, these agencies were requested to actively participate in the Mountain
Pass security engineering and activities. This document describes the security activities,
program, tasks, and roles that were developed and implemented for the Mountain Pass

The system development methodology that was followed at EPIC was a tailored analyze-design-plan-implement approach. First, a detailed functional analysis of the EPIC environment was conducted. The current EPIC environment was analyzed to determine how, why, when, where, and what tasks were being performed, who performed the tasks, and what products were prepared. Specifically, the analysis included a review of all system-related documents, interviews with current and proposed users and system specialists, and observation ofthe current system operation. The result of the functional analysis was a recommended Functional Architecture which addressed EPICs functional requirements and alternative design concepts.

Using the Functional Architecture, the Mountain Pass Project team used a COTS integration approach that allowed the system architects and engineers to quickly define and implement a low risk development strategy. This was necessary because of the extremely tight schedule for completing the project. Additional principles applied to the Mountain Pass Project were to:
Build on existing capabilities where feasible
Implement the obvious (high value, low risk) Use proven solutions Use standard protocols and interfaces
Emphasize COTS integration versus research and development solutions
Design to accommodate projected growth in database size, external system access, and user population
The key Mountain Pass Project architectural decisions were to:
Utilize a client-server processing model with: Centralized, specialized servers Distributed workstations
Install separate Secret and Sensitive local area networks (LANs) with a low-to-high security guard separating the two regions
Require software that met the C2 functionality as defined in 5200.28-STD, The Trusted Computer System Evaluation Criteria (TCSEC). Specifically, Mountain Pass required:
Installation of a C2-compliant multi-tasking operating system for workstations and servers

In addition, the security architecture was limited by the following two constraints: (1) existing policies for the safeguarding of Sensitive and Classified information and (2) the availability of technology to segregate data at different classification levels.

The Mountain Pass security architecture was implemented in two phases. In Phase I, the basic capabilities were provided to two pilot workgroups at EPIC. In Phase 11, these capabilities were incrementally expanded and tailored to other workgroups. Also, in Phase II, four major upgrades were added: automated login, multi-database query, DBMS, and the EPIC Guard. Both phases were completed in approximately eighteen months.

Security engineering (including C&A) for Mountain Pass was included as part ofthe system engineering life cycle. Due to the extremely tight schedule for implementing Mountain Pass, the security engineering tasks were developed and executed concurrently with the system design and development activities. In addition, the security engineering tasks were performed in parallel, specifically, development of a security architecture, definition of security requirements, and preparation of a System Security Plan (SSP).

2.3 FIPS PUB 102 Certification and Accreditation (C&A) Process

The EIS certification process was based on the process defined in FIPS PUB 102, Guidelinefor Computer Security Certification cmdAccreditation. This standard was used because EPIC is primarily authorized and staffed by Federal civil agencies and the National Institute of Standards and Technology (MST) is responsible for providing guidance for civil agencies that process Sensitive information.

As defined in FIPS PUB 102, the certification efifort is divided into basic evaluation and detailed evaluation. The general distinction between basic and detailed evaluations is that basic evaluation focuses on the overall security functionality. Detailed evaluation focuses on whether specific security features work correctly, satisfy performance criteria, and acceptably resist penetration. The certification process is an iterative process, with previous stages being reentered and the work repeated. For example, during basic evaluation/RAVA, a new security function may be identified that had not been previously documented. Development of a new security function may require a revision to the security boundary defined in the planning stage and repetition ofthe data collection stages. At the completion of the certification tests, the formal acceptance of system
security by the is based on the Security Evaluation Report/Certification Report of Findings
and the documentation developed during the system engineering life cycle stages. The for EIS was the Deputy Administrator of DEA.

Due to the nature ofDEA's mission and the sensitivity of its data, evaluating system security, implementing appropriate safeguards, and certifying systems are a vital part of DEA's system life cycle development process. Due to EPIC's mission and the sensitivity of its data, security was also important to the agencies that participate at EPIC.
Certification of the EIS involved a technical assessment of the security features/functionality to

determine the extent that these features met the EIS and security requirements and applicable security policies (e.g., DOJ, Executive Orders (E.O.s), Privacy Act). Certification also included executing security tests to demonstrate the adequacy of the security features and requirements. Accreditation ofthe EIS was a management decision by the Deputy Administrator

of to operate the EIS in a specific operational environment. The objective of the efifort was to accredit the EIS as a partitioned system, physically separated into two regions: a Sensitive region and a Classified region, with a low-to-high security guard connecting the two regions.

2.5 Functional Description of Mountain Pass CertiHcation Tasks

The certification process described below is a functional description based on the Mountain Pass Project, specifying what must be done and a general description of how the tasks are to be accomplished. It does not present a detailed, step-by-step procedure for performing the certification tasks. Although the tasks are specific to Mountain Pass, the general approach is applicable to other system efforts.

Planning Stage: In the planning stage, the focus was on understanding the specific application and the certification process. The following questions provided the focus for defining the planning stage tasks. These questions were derived from FTPS PUB 102.
What are the goals of the Mountain Pass project and EIS? Where are the major anticipated problem areas and areas of emphasis?
What other resources are needed to complete the effort, for example, technical tools, independent contractor to perform testing (verification and validation),
Is documentation available that describes EIS and its controls?
What are the applicable external policies and requirements, including laws, regulations, standards, and guidelines?
What are the applicable internal policies and requirements, quality assurance standards, test procedures, documentation standards, and audit standards?

What are the boundaries for this certification? A general guideline is that the certification boundary includes all the relevant components of the application (EIS), including the administrative, physical, procedural, and technical features.
What is the level of detail required in the Certification Report of Findings/SSP?
In response to the questions listed above, the following tasks addressed the effort:
Reviewed the background information necessary to understand the proposed EIS. This activity included a high-level review of the current and proposed EIS to understand the system and the issues.
Reviewed the applicable Federal, DOJ, and DEA security policies, procedures, and regulations. DEA documents focused on implementing the DOJ and Federal regulations.
Defined the scope of the effort and developed the Plan.
Assigned responsibilities and developed a schedule for completing the C&A tasks. The C&A tasks were divided among several organizations:
Proposed a methodology to be used for completing the certification and accreditation. PTPS PUB 102 was the primary reference document.
Ensured that the Mountain Pass SSP followed the format specified in Office of
Management and Budget (0MB) Bulletin 90-08, Guidance for Preparation of Security Plans for Federal Computer Systems that Contain Sensitive Information.

Data Collection: In data collection, the focus was on building on the base of knowledge acquired during the planning stage, for example, documenting additional security requirements identified by the users. The following questions, based on FIPS PUB 102, focused the EIS data collection effort:
What is the functionality provided at each implementation phase of Mountain Pass. Specifically, what are the security technical capabilities implemented in each phase?
What are the security requirements for the EIS and what is the planned implementation by phase?
What is the system architecture for EIS and the flow of information within and external to EIS?
What is the EIS Mountain Pass security architecture?

Documented the functionality provided in each phase of the Mountain Pass effort.

DOJ, DEA, DOD, and DISA shared the responsibility for the conduct of the Mountain Pass Project. The management approach followed was a collaborative Senior Management Team, made up of members of the four participating organizations, to provide overall direction and oversight of project activities. A PM, assisted by a Deputy and a project staff, directed the day-to-day activities of the project.

At the working level, the project was composed of a System Engineering Team and an Integration Team. Each team was led by a government Team Chief. Finally, a Transition Team composed of EPIC personnel assisted in the transition of system management and support from the project team to EPIC at the completion of the project.
Approximately 80% of the project activity was planned to take place at EPIC. Ideally, both

The Computer Security Act of 1987 (Public Law 100-235) requires that all Federal computer systems that contain Sensitive information implement a plan for the security and privacy of these
Bulletin 90-08 provides guidance for the preparation of computer security plans.
The objectives of the security planning process, as described in Bulletin 90-08, are to identify and assess:
The nature and extent of Sensitive information systems and the security requirements of such systems
The adequacy ofthe administrative, management, and technical approaches used in protecting Sensitive systems
Responsibilities and accountability for the security of Sensitive systems
Requirements for additional guidance, standards, assistance, training, and new technology to improve the protection of Sensitive information resources.
Appendix of Bulletin 90-08 was used as the fundamental outline for documenting the EIS SSP.
The EIS SSP described the security requirements essential to protecting the information
processed in the EIS and outlined the activities used to determine if these requirements were adequately satisfied.
The EIS SSP was developed incrementally and modified as the program progressed. It documented the security requirements, architectural decisions, technical controls implementation,

Individuals representing all agencies participating in the EPIC project were interviewed to identify the primary lessons learned during the development and acquisition process. These lessons learned are divided into two areas: management and technical and are summarized in sections 5. and 5.2. Activities/processes that worked well and those that did not are included.

Senior Management Team: The SMT functioned as the planning and decision-making group responsible for ensuring adherence to the Mountain Pass activities. The SMT provided the appropriate level of management authority and political clout to make decisions and ensure that the project progressed on schedule and within budget. The SMT was an effective organization because it provided significant management oversight and made decisions when requested. For example, the SMT was very responsive to the PM's needs and requests for formal direction.
Program Management: The was an effective manager of a multitude of simultaneous

contracts and contractors, and government personnel. The enthusiastically participated in and encouraged the exchange of information among the various Mountain Pass participants, worked effectively with the SMT in resolving issues and recommending solutions, and clearly communicated the dehvery dates and products needed. This kept the project on schedule and within budget. Having an on-site coordinator (the Deputy PM) was extremely important because it facilitated the early identification of problems and their rapid resolution. It also provided the on-site teams with the appropriate level of authority and guidance necessary to ensure decisions were made and implemented correctly.
Accreditation Working Group (AWG): The facilitated communications between
participants and helped to raise security issues early. great deal of informal communications
between members helped to get issues raised and solved in an open environment. All meetings were well documented and information was always readily available and distributed to
all participants. The was a key success factor because all members actively participated,

were energetic and positive, and caused necessary actions to happen quickly. provided significant technical expertise when requested, resulting in well-informed discussions and decisions at the meetings. Another critical success factor was continuity of the membership - the
majority of the members participated fi'om the beginning to the end of the Mountain Pass Project and members who were replaced were provided with all the documentation to bring them up to speed.

critical lesson learned was that it was important to keep the personnel fi'om all the participating agencies actively involved. This active involvement helped with the agency buy-in to the selected security policies, requirements, and features.
Certification Working Group (CWG): This group was established to provide technical
guidance and recommendations to the and the contractors. However, because most ofthe CWG members also participated in the AWG, this group met only a couple oftimes. At times,
the meetings were lengthy because a detailed analysis of an issue with recommended alternatives was not provided. These analyses should have been developed by the CWG.
Systems Engineering Team: The Systems Engineering team facilitated and coordinated
meetings and communications between the developers, users, and the and they provided the integration contractor with valuable technical direction.

Integration Contractor: The integration contractor was provided a detailed system design and, therefore, was able to develop a relatively rapid COTS solution. They were responsive to the sponsor and the users in modifying the implementation to provide an acceptable user interface. One of the major lessons learned was that the implementation of the security features should have occurred much earlier in the implementation effort. This resulted in a crunch in the schedule and less time to complete the RAVA and ST&E tasks.
Memorandums of Understanding (MOUs): The MOU process was the most difficult problem
for the members to finish. Even with extensive information sharing, it appeared that there were many distinct differences in the way law enforcement agencies protect information. There
were no consistent information processing standards for law enforcement agencies. The
should have been started sooner (at the beginning of the project) when all the
representatives were initially selected. Also, the process was impacted by the requirement to have the agreements signed by the agency legal representatives. This extended the time to completion.

The purpose of this letter is to inform you of the activities I have initiated that will require your personal support.

The Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) embarked on a project to modernize and improve the El Paso Intelligence Center’s (EPIC) information processing capability. This project is called the Mountain Pass Project and involves your agency. The objective of the
with an improved, integrated, and automated information

project is to provide the system in 1992. The EPIC Information System (EIS) is intended to meet or exceed current information processing needs of DEA/EPIC and participating agencies, as well as provide the infrastructure from which information system requirements may be met.

It is not the intention of this project to alter or disrupt the information sharing relationships that had been established between the DEA/EPIC and the participating agencies. These relationships have served the countemarcotics efforts well and were deemed to be mutually beneficial to all DEA/EPIC participating agencies. However, we will need to properly document these information sharing relationships which developed and evolved informally over the years.

An important part of this project is the information systems certification and accreditation (C&A) process that is required by 0MB Circular A- 130. Certification is the technical evaluation of a system (the EIS in this case) to determine how effectively it meets information security requirements. Accreditation is the acknowledgment and acceptance of residual information security risks and the decision and authorization to operate the system in the manner for which it was intended. In order to ensure that the needed information security posture is achieved, a Certification Working Group (CWG) and an Accreditation Working Group (AWG) have been established. The CWG, for the most part, consists of technical experts who will assess risks to the EIS, analyze the vulnerabilities of the EIS, and recommend balanced actions to mitigate information security weaknesses.
The purpose of the is to ensure that the information security concerns of all agencies that provide information to the DEA/EPIC are adequately addressed in the EIS. To meet this
objective, the is briefed monthly and from an information security standpoint, monitors the progress of the Mountain Pass Project and the results of the certification process. In
addition, the representatives are requested to provide input and feedback from their
agencies on the topics discussed at the monthly meetings. The representatives are also
asked to raise any issues that may impact on the timely accreditation of the EIS.

The Committee is established by the Administrator, DEA, to fulfill the need to assure that information security requirements are maintained and enhanced throughout the continued technological enhancements of countemarcotics information systems.

The purpose of the Committee is to review, recommend, monitor, and advise on major security considerations due to technology changes in information systems development. This includes evaluating the extent to which these changes will be implemented and describing the security implications of these changes. The Committee is responsible for developing a strategy to assure that security methods, techniques, plans, and procedures keep pace with the changing technology and that security continues to be an integral element in the planning and implementation of all future systems.

This Committee will have the authority to review, recommend, and monitor the initiatives and changes that are planned or that have occurred. The Committee members will be the voting authority representing the interests of their agency on major technological changes and reaccreditation of current systems.

DEA will provide the permanent Chairperson of this group. The membership shall include, but is not limited to, representatives from the following departments and agencies... The Chairperson may also, from time to time, invite visitors to provide information of interest to the Committee.
The activities and responsibilities of the Committee shall include reviewing the methodology to identify, describe, and assess major technology changes and their impact on the security of

shared countemarcotics systems and developing a strategy to assure that security methods, techniques, plans, and procedures keep pace and that security requirements continue to be an integral part of the system development.

As scheduled by the Chairperson, the Committee shall meet at least semi-annually. The Committee shall convene at the call of the Chairperson or upon request to the Chairperson by a majority of the members. Each participating department or agency shall be entitled to a single vote. An alternate for each voting member shall be designated to act in the absence of the principal. Issues before the Committee for vote shall be decided by simple majority of the voters present.
The Committee shall be supported by the members of Offices which shall provide all required policy and administrative support. The duties and responsibilities of the assigned support staff include:
Provide direct support to the Chairperson
Prepare, coordinate, and disseminate meeting agendas, notices of meetings, current membership rosters, minutes, and summaries of other reports
On behalf of the Chairperson, organize, direct, manage, and record Committee activities
Assist the Chairperson in identifying, articulating, presenting, and developing pertinent issues and recommendations

This charter shall become effective upon the signature of the Chairperson and shall remain in effect for n years from the effective date or until the Committee’s purpose has been accomplished, whichever occurs first. At the end of the period, this charter shall be reviewed.
